p.src: Overview: A horizon is not merely a causal boundary. For a stationary observer it is a thermal system: a thermometer held a proper distance $\rho$ from the horizon reads a temperature of order $1/(2\pi\rho)$, while gravitational redshift makes the radiation seen far away much colder. We shall carry this black-hole lesson into de Sitter space, derive the fixed horizon radius $H^{-1}$, and write the observer’s static-patch metric. The second half of the lecture follows the thermodynamics to its unsettling consequences: finite de Sitter entropy, Poincare recurrences, Boltzmann brains, eternal inflation, and the measure problem. A final discussion separates the exact supersymmetric structures of string theory from the still-unknown framework that might describe our world.

p.src: The first experiment is local. Hold a thermometer at fixed proper distance $\rho$ from any smooth, nonextremal horizon. Close enough to the horizon, the geometry has the universal Rindler form, and the thermometer reads $T_{\rm local}(\rho)\simeq \frac{1}{2\pi\rho}$ in units with $\hbar=c=k_B=1$. Restoring constants gives $k_B T_{\rm local}(\rho)\simeq \frac{\hbar c}{2\pi\rho}.$ The divergence as $\rho\to0$ does not mean that an infalling observer encounters an ordinary material furnace. It is the temperature assigned by an observer who remains stationary just outside the horizon and must therefore accelerate ever more violently.

The drawing seems to make the patch shrink toward the future, but coordinate width is not proper distance. On a constant-$\eta$ slice the squared physical distance between the observer at $x=0$ and the horizon at $x=\Delta x$ is $D^2=\frac{(\Delta x)^2}{H^2\eta^2}.$ The horizon is a $45^\circ$ null line ending at $\eta=0$, hence $\Delta x=\lvert\eta\rvert.$ Substitution gives $D_{\rm hor}^2=\frac{1}{H^2},
\qquad
D_{\rm hor}=\frac{1}{H}.$ The coordinate separation shrinks, but the conformal factor grows by exactly the compensating amount. The proper horizon radius is constant.

zh: 经典的从外部进行的描述类似于人们熟悉的黑洞故事。位于中心的Bob看着Alice远去。她的信号红移越来越强，到达得越来越慢；她看起来被压扁在视界上，并最终消失。后来的旅行者Jane则表现为边界附近沉积层中的又一层更薄的层。

p.src: Boltzmann Brains and Typical Observers

u.src: Boltzmann Brains and Typical Observers
en: Boltzmann Brains and Typical Observers
ja: ボルツマン脳と典型的観測者
zh: 玻尔兹曼大脑与典型观测者

p.src: Suppose a thermal fluctuation creates an entire big-bang-like state. That requires an enormous entropy decrease. A fluctuation producing one solar system is cheaper; an already warm Earth is cheaper still. If the only requirement is one observer, the least costly fluctuation might create only a functioning brain complete with apparent memories. Such a hypothetical observer is called a Boltzmann brain.

A fluctuation producing one solar system is cheaper; an already warm Earth is cheaper still. If the only requirement is one observer, the least costly fluctuation might create only a functioning brain complete with apparent memories. Such a hypothetical observer is called a Boltzmann brain.
en: Suppose a thermal fluctuation creates an entire big-bang-like state. That requires an enormous entropy decrease. A fluctuation producing one solar system is cheaper; an already warm Earth is cheaper still. If the only requirement is one observer, the least costly fluctuation might create only a functioning brain complete with apparent memories. Such a hypothetical observer is called a Boltzmann brain.
ja: 熱的な揺らぎがビッグバンのような状態全体を創り出すと仮定しよう。それには膨大なエントロピー減少が必要である。一つの太陽系を生み出す揺らぎはより安価であり、すでに暖かい地球はさらに安価である。唯一の要件が一人の観測者であるならば、最も費用のかからない揺らぎは、見かけの記憶を備えた機能する脳だけを創り出すかもしれない。そのような仮説的観測者はボルツマン脳と呼ばれる。
zh: 假设一次热涨落创造出一个完整的类大爆炸状态。那需要巨大的熵减少。产生一个太阳系的涨落代价更低；一个已经温暖的 Earth 代价还要更低。如果唯一的要求是一个观测者，那么代价最低的涨落可能只创造出一个功能完备的大脑，并带有看似真实的记忆。这样一个假想的观测者被称为玻尔兹曼大脑。

p.src: The issue is not whether one bizarre fluctuation is logically possible. It is whether a cosmological model predicts that almost every observer is such a fluctuation. We reason from our observations by assuming that we are not fantastically atypical. A theory in which ordinary observers with coherent cosmic histories are exponentially outnumbered by isolated thermal brains undermines that inference.

u.src: The issue is not whether one bizarre fluctuation is logically possible. It is whether a cosmological model predicts that almost every observer is such a fluctuation. We reason from our observations by assuming that we are not fantastically atypical. A theory in which ordinary observers with coherent cosmic histories are exponentially outnumbered by isolated thermal brains undermines that inference.
en: The issue is not whether one bizarre fluctuation is logically possible. It is whether a cosmological model predicts that almost every observer is such a fluctuation. We reason from our observations by assuming that we are not fantastically atypical. A theory in which ordinary observers with coherent cosmic histories are exponentially outnumbered by isolated thermal brains undermines that inference.
ja: 問題は、一つの奇妙な揺らぎが論理的に可能かどうかではない。ある宇宙論的モデルが、ほとんどすべての観測者はそのような揺らぎであると予測するかどうかである。我々は、自分たちが途方もなく非典型的であるとは仮定しないことによって、観測から推論する。首尾一貫した宇宙史を持つ通常の観測者が、孤立した熱的脳によって指数関数的に圧倒される理論は、その推論を損なう。
zh: 问题不在于某一次奇异的涨落在逻辑上是否可能。而在于一个宇宙学模型是否预言几乎每一个观测者都是这样的涨落。我们从观测出发进行推理时，假设我们并非极其非典型。如果一个理论中具有连贯宇宙历史的普通观测者被孤立的熱大脑以指数方式超过，那就削弱了这一推断。

p.src: The Boltzmann-brain problem therefore names a quantitative consistency test. One compares the expected abundance of ordinary observers with the abundance of fluctuation-born observers. If the latter dominate, either the vacuum must decay before they proliferate, the measure must be changed, or the cosmological assumptions must be reconsidered.

p.src: To expose the statistical difficulty, Susskind first leaves cosmology and considers an exponentially growing human population with finite but unknown resources. Assume that observers are typical among all people who ever live. If the population doubles every generation and then ends, half of all people live in the last generation, three quarters in the last two, and seven eighths in the last three: $f_n=1-2^{-n}.$ Typicality would then place us uncomfortably near the end, even though we know nothing about the total resource supply. This is not offered as a reliable prediction of human extinction. It is a warning that exponential growth makes counts dominated by the cutoff.

zh: 回答: 许多近似构造研究超对称破缺，但恰恰缺少的是完全可控的非超对称骨架。人们可以在作出标准近似之后进行计算，却并不总是知道这些近似所趋近的精确对象是什么。

zh: 回答: 不。它确立的是，观测到的世界并非仅由精确的超对称部分描述。它既未证明也未否证这一部分与一个包含现实物理的更大理论相关联。

zh: 讲座以稳健的数学核心与尚未完成的物理外推之间的这一区分作结。这并不是断言该核心无用，也不是声称该外推已经确立。它陈述的是精确知识止于何处。
